record.context_brief: segment representations of three-colourable planar graphs
record.original_question: Is every 3-colourable planar graph representable by intersecting line segments, without any restriction on slopes?

evidence.quote: Question 8.5 Is every 3-colourable planar graph representable by intersecting line segments, regardless of slopes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A simple finite graph $G=(V,E)$ is said to have a segment representation if there exists an assignment $v \mapsto S_v$ of each vertex $v\in V$ to a closed line segment $S_v\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, for any two distinct vertices $u,v\in V$, the segments $S_u$ and $S_v$ have non-empty intersection if and only if $uv\in E$. The slopes of the segments are not constrained and may be arbitrary.

A graph $G$ is $3$-colourable if its vertices can be partitioned into three independent sets, and it is planar if it admits an embedding in $\mathbb{R}^2$ without edge crossings.

Question: Does every $3$-colourable planar graph admit a segment representation (with no restriction on the set of slopes used)?
artifact.status_search_result: The stronger form of this question — that every 3-colourable planar graph has a segment intersection representation using only 3 slopes — was proved by Castro, Gonçalves and Ochem (WG 2019, with extended version on arXiv:2511.20368 and HAL). This in particular answers the unrestricted-slope version affirmatively. The fully general Scheinerman conjecture (all planar graphs are segment intersection graphs) was earlier established by Chalopin and Gonçalves (2009), which also implies the result for the 3-colourable case.

status_evidence.title: 3-Colorable Planar Graphs Have an Intersection Segment Representation Using 3 Slopes
status_evidence.snippet: Scheinerman conjectured that for 3-colorable planar graphs the slopes can be restricted to 3, proved by the authors.
status_evidence.claim: 3-colourable planar graphs admit segment representations (in fact with only 3 slopes).

status_evidence.title: 3-colorable planar graphs have an intersection segment representation using 3 slopes (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Extended version proving every 3-colorable planar graph has a 3-slope segment intersection representation.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative resolution of the unrestricted-slope question.

status_evidence.title: Scheinerman's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Chalopin and Gonçalves proved that every planar graph is an intersection graph of line segments in the plane.
status_evidence.claim: The general planar case (hence the 3-colourable case) is solved.
